p: Get started with Quilzo in ten minutes
x: From nothing to a running admin, a published site and your first agent, in the order Quilzo needs them. Quilzo is a self-hosted control plane for AI agents. Each agent has a declaration saying what it may do, and one gate enforces it on every action. A person decides on the actions that matter, and every run is recorded in a signed log. It ships as a single program with no dependencies. This guide takes about ten minutes. You need a terminal on Linux, macOS or Windows. A model is optional: an agent can walk its declaration without one, and you can connect a model at the end.

p: Glossary: AI agents, MCP, A2A and the words Quilzo uses
x: AI agent control planeThe layer that decides what AI agents may do: identity, policy, budgets, approvals, and an audit trail of every action, enforced outside the model. p: Limits that hold: what a hijacked AI agent still cannot do
x: The declaration is enforced by code outside the model, so it holds however the model is persuaded. Prompt injection is text an agent reads that tells it to do something its user did not ask for. No classifier reliably tells those words from honest content. Quilzo does not try to: it limits what a run can do, records what it read, and stops for a person when private material and somebody else's words meet an outbound call.

p: Run an AI agent's own code in a sandbox
x: When an agent's own program decides instead of a model, Quilzo runs it in a box and hands in only what the declaration allows. A program is the other way an agent decides: a coding agent's command line, a script, or a runtime somebody built their agent in. Quilzo never runs it as itself. It runs it in a box with no capabilities, its own namespaces, Landlock for files and ports, and a system call filter. It hands in three things over the box's own loopback: the agent interface for this run, a model endpoint through the gateway, and a proxy to the declared hosts.

p: LLM gateway: model routes, budgets in money and a privacy guard
x: One gateway for every model call: which model answers, what each caller may spend, and what may leave in a prompt. The model gateway is where every model call from Quilzo goes: agents, chatbots, the writing assistant, analyst triage, and agents' own programs. It tries routes in order, charges each call to a caller at that route's prices, holds callers to their budgets, and masks personal data before a prompt reaches a route that may not receive it. Prompts are never recorded, only who asked, which route answered, and how much.
